newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Smithkline Beecham six month net up.
newsitem.headline: India's Smithkline Beecham six month net up.

text.p: India's Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd said on Thursday its net profit in the six months ending June 30 rose by 19.3 percent to 252 million rupees.

The company in a statement said the board of directors had announced an interim dividend of 20 percent payable on the increased equity of the company resulting from a 3:5 bonus declared earlier this year.
The statement said the turnover of the company in the six months ending June 30, 1997, grew by 565 million rupees, a 27 percent increase over the same period a year ago.
It said gross operating profit grew by 13.6 percent.
Britain's Smithkline Beecham Plc has a 40 percent stake in the Indian company.

In March the Indian firm offered three bonus shasres for every five held after its net profit jumped 30 percent to 469.4 million in calendar 1996. In 1996 the company announced two interim dividends totalling 60 percent.

"I believe that with the investments we are currently making in new products and product categories, the company is about to enter an era of explosive growth which will continue well into the next decade," SBCH Managing Director Simon Scarff said in a statement.
